ruleRoutingGuidance.belongs: the browser dashboard over Claudinite scheduler state and the site that publishes it
ruleRoutingGuidance.excludes: how the scheduler behaves — core; workflow practice — git-github; product sites — public-website

pitch: Gives the repo a read-only web page showing what its automated Claude work is doing: what is stuck, what is queued, what has already run, and what the rules and checks have been costing and catching. It can also cover a whole fleet of repositories from one overview. Two scheduled tasks keep it live, one republishing the page to GitHub Pages whenever its sources change and one deploying the sign-in endpoint, and neither reports success until the deployed result actually answers.

questions.prompt: Is this deployment this repo's OWN dashboard, or the fleet overview across many repos? A fleet deployment also names an "owner", whose repos are enumerated in the browser as the viewer, and optionally an "exclude" list.
questions.distill: set config.mode to "repo" or "fleet" — there is no default and the build refuses to publish without it; a "fleet" answer must come with config.owner, and a "repo" answer with none; never write repos, rosterFile, rosterUrl or canonRepo, which the build refuses

adoptionHandover.step: Enable GitHub Pages with source "GitHub Actions" — this repo's /settings/pages
adoptionHandover.breaks: the publish-pages task pushes the build, and its deploy run then fails — the task parks at needs-human-action naming this
adoptionHandover.done: the Pages URL serves the dashboard, and a publish-pages run converged done

adoptionHandover.step: Turn on Sign in with GitHub — the pack README's "Turning sign-in on" is that checklist.
adoptionHandover.breaks: nobody can read the dashboard at all: sign-in is the only way in, so until the pair is set the page shows its gate saying this deployment is not finished being set up, naming the two variables
adoptionHandover.done: a signed-in viewer sees the rate pill read “…/5000 · user”
